events.title: Star violinist Anne-Sophie Mutter: 50 years on stage
events.summary: Anne-Sophie Mutter constantly reinvents herself. For her 50th onstage anniversary, the star violinist is surprising audiences with sounds from around the world and never-before-recorded commissions.

events.title: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
events.summary: "Immune hubs" that actively defend the brain have been discovered in mouse skull marrow. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

events.title: Spiraling health costs force Iranians to delay care
events.summary: A single chemotherapy session in Iran can cost six times the monthly minimum wage. As drug prices soar and medicine is in short supply, doctors say more patients are delaying or abandoning treatment.

events.title: Could Russia's growing fuel crisis help end the Ukraine war?
events.summary: Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries have deepened Russia's fuel crisis, with shortages reaching Moscow. Could growing public anger put Putin under pressure?

events.title: Ukraine: Zelenskyy rejects wartime elections
events.summary: The Ukrainian president says wartime elections, as called for by the ex-defense minister, could "split Ukraine." He also said Russia was planning to mobilize hundreds of thousands of troops after September polls there.

events.title: What is the 'political firewall' against Germany's far-right AfD?
events.summary: Germany's centrist parties reject any cooperation with the Alternative for Germany (AfD), parts of which are classified as right-wing extremist. However, this policy is coming under increasing pressure.

events.title: Sydney Marathon medal wrongly shows German landmark
events.summary: A medal minted for finishers in the Sydney Marathon features a skyline of the city — with one landmark from rather far away. Organizers say the muddle only makes the medal "a little more unique."

events.title: Could Ukraine's Mykhailo Fedorov challenge Zelenskyy?
events.summary: An explosive video released last week by Ukraine's former defense minister spoke of corruption, a crisis of leadership and elections. What could follow?

events.title: Spain battles forest fire a short drive from flash flood
events.summary: The blaze, near Valencia, forced more than 1,000 people from their homes. In nearby Catalonia, civil defense teams carried out 200 rescue operations after floods trapped residents in cars and homes.

events.title: Small German airplane crashes in Croatia, killing 2
events.summary: The two-seater motor glider went down in the Velebit mountains, near Zadar, killing both passengers.

events.title: Germany investigates arms cache found in woods near Berlin
events.summary: Handguns and ammunition were found in a forest near Berlin last year. Reports say German authorities suspect they were to be used for assassinations on behalf of Russian intelligence.

events.title: Industry and residents clash over water near Berlin
events.summary: The state surrounding Berlin is drying out, but local Tesla and Red Bull plants are looking to expand. Is Brandenburg running out of water to share?

events.title: 'Masha and the Bear': Ukraine sanctions Russian cartoon
events.summary: Ukraine has imposed sanctions on the hit Russian children's cartoon "Masha and the Bear," a step towards banning it. The culture minister called the show propaganda. Russia said the move showed Kyiv's "ugly nature."

events.title: What to do when wildfires trigger trauma
events.summary: The wildfires this summer have broken records in Germany and are unlikely to subside in future. Psychologists say post-traumatic stress disorder caused by such disasters is serious but can be treated if people seek help.

events.title: Bauhaus Manifesto: Broad alliance promoting artistic freedom
events.summary: Weeks before Saxony-Anhalt's state election, representatives from German cultural, crafts, architecture, design and church sectors unite to promote freedom, openness and creativity.

events.title: Ronaldinho to make football comeback aged 46
events.summary: More than a decade after his last professional appearance, Brazilian superstar Ronaldinho is set for a comeback. The former world player of the year is to play in Italy’s third tier.

events.title: Why Germany's gas storage levels are so low
events.summary: Germany's gas storage facilities are only 50% full as traders bet that wholesale prices will fall if the Iran war ends. With around three months until winter, DW asks whether the country can refill its reserves in time.

events.title: Munich prosecutors close fatal 1970 antisemitic arson case
events.summary: Prosecutors and police in Munich believe they have identified the man who set a 1970 fire at a Jewish community center and old people's home that killed seven people. But he died in 2020, so prosecution is not possible.

events.title: How Europe can better protect against extreme wildfires
events.summary: In another summer of European wildfires that have even seen wetlands burning, scientists say the situation is set to worsen in the future. What's needed is fire prevention and climate protection.

events.title: Bernadette Amani 'living her dream' at Bayern Munich
events.summary: Bernadette Amani is heading into her first full season with Bayern Munich, having joined the club in January. Making a living at football is something she never imagined possible while growing up in rural Ivory Coast.

events.title: Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan sentenced to life in prison
events.summary: A Chinese court ordered the former billionaire's assets to be confiscated and fined Evergrande-related companies billions of dollars.

events.title: Germany condemns Israeli minister's Gaza 'killings' remarks
events.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has denounced a call by Israel's far-right security minister to carry out "targeted killings" of Palestinians in Gaza. The outrage spans the entire political spectrum.

events.title: Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala collapses on pitch again
events.summary: One of Germany's top footballers has collapsed on the pitch for a second time in four days ahead of the new season. Bayern Munich's Jamal Musiala has said he has a "neurological dysfunction" that causes blackouts.

events.title: Germany news: Minister wants to help renters to install AC
events.summary: The justice minister wants to make it easier for tenants to install air conditioning or external blinds. Meanwhile, a defense CEO is reportedly in hiding after being warned of Russian plots to kill him.

events.title: Who really owns the Caspian Sea?
events.summary: Five countries border the Caspian Sea, but none owns a fixed share. A 2018 convention established rules for navigation, security and fishing while leaving some seabed borders unresolved.

events.title: Messi retirement hint highlights football era nearing an end
events.summary: Soon after propelling Argentina to a second consecutive World Cup final, Lionel Messi has cast some doubt on his future. While retirement doesn't seem imminent, it still beckons for him and Cristiano Ronaldo.

events.title: In drought-stricken France, tankers supply drinking water
events.summary: France is seeing water shortages in regions that usually have plenty of supply. This summer's extreme heat is exposing how unprepared much of the country, and Europe, is for increasing water scarcity.

events.title: Will Germany's drought push up food prices?
events.summary: Germany's main farmers' association has warned of a below-average harvest after drought and crops damaged by extreme heat. DW looks into what lower yields could mean for food prices and grocery bills.

events.title: Dressed for power: Giorgia Meloni and the language of fashion
events.summary: From Giorgia Meloni's shift from dark suits to pastels to Angela Merkel's signature jackets, politicians have long used clothing to shape how voters see them. In this day and age, power dressing has evolved.

events.title: How to grow food for more people in a hotter world
events.summary: Inside futuristic labs, plants are scanned, stressed and analyzed. The aim is to use the results to produce plant strains that can better serve a growing population in a warming world.

events.title: How Germany's Hyrox became a global fitness craze
events.summary: Created in Germany and now a global success, Hyrox combines running and functional training into a unique format. How a German concept became an international sports phenomenon.

events.title: Do not inhale! How wildfire smoke 'affects the whole body'
events.summary: Wildfires destroy lives and livelihoods. But survivors and firefighters also suffer long-term harm to their health. A growing body of research suggests particulate matter (PM2.5) in wildfire smoke is a major culprit.

events.title: Norway wealth fund sounds alarm on AI stock market bubble
events.summary: The head of Norway's sovereign wealth fund has warned that soaring AI-driven stock valuations could trigger a sharp correction. How exposed is the world's largest sovereign wealth fund to a market downturn?

events.title: Can the cool north handle a surge in climate tourism?
events.summary: With heat records continually being broken and southern summers getting hotter, travelers are heading north. Fragile ecosystems are paying the price.

events.title: Fatty food raises risk of colorectal cancer
events.summary: Did you know fatty foods can increase production of an acid in your gut that promotes tumor growth? That's on top of all the other health risks linked to fatty foods, like fries and burgers.

events.title: Why women are breaking men's endurance records
events.summary: Sophie Woods has completed the 2,000-kilometer Via Alpina faster even than the fastest-ever man. DW explains why she is not the only woman breaking men's records in extreme sports.

events.title: Hunger stones: The history behind 'if you see me, weep'
events.summary: Centuries-old hunger stones are emerging as Europe's rivers recede. Among the most famous is the Decin hunger stone in the Elbe River with its cryptic message.

events.title: Can a drug help prevent trauma? Study with mice suggests so
events.summary: Researchers in Munich and Stockholm blocked the lifelong social cost of early adversity in mice with a single compound. The catch: it only worked when given during the trauma, not after.

events.title: Can we go green without forever chemicals?
events.summary: As nations globally move to ban forever chemicals, should renewable energy technologies be exempt for the sake of saving the climate?

events.title: Eurovision bars countries at war from hosting
events.summary: A Eurovision victory will no longer guarantee hosting rights if war or a wider security crisis affects the winning country. The change could have particular significance for recent high-flyers Ukraine and Israel.

events.title: Mozart tribute ends on sour note after mass figurine theft
events.summary: A playful tribute to Mozart has turned into a whodunit after 210 gold-colored figures disappeared from one of Austria's busiest tourist spots. The mass theft forced organizers to end the outdoor display early.

events.title: EU waste packaging rules: Why small businesses are worried
events.summary: The EU has introduced new rules targeting packaging waste and "forever chemicals." Although the changes will be phased in slowly, some small sellers have already paused shipments due to the additional red tape.

events.title: AI helping create popular mobile sports games
events.summary: After the World Cup and before the domestic season, many fans still crave more football. Amateur coders are helping to fill this gap.

events.title: Solar eclipse: What to look forward to
events.summary: The last solar eclipse visible from the European mainland was in 1999. Here's what to expect, and how to prepare for this rare occasion.

events.title: Making sense of Trump's executive order on US vaccinations
events.summary: President Donald Trump and his Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. have long tried to reduce the number of vaccinations available to the US public and even farm animals. The latest move in context.

events.title: How one German city plans to challenge climate extremes
events.summary: Western Europe has recorded its hottest-ever June and July, and extreme weather from drought to storms is here to stay. How can we adapt to a fundamentally altered climate? Cities like Kiel are trying new ideas.

events.title: How the Rhine drought threatens Germany's economic recovery
events.summary: Germany's inland waterways still move around 5% of the nation's goods. With the Rhine at a critically low level, DW explores how the drought is hitting the economy where it hurts most.

events.title: UEFA, other football federations unite against Infantino
events.summary: A few weeks ago, Gianni Infantino looked set for another unopposed term as FIFA president. Now, with an election looming, the beleagured football executive is counting the numbers and could be hanging by a thread.

events.title: Type 2 diabetes in young women increasingly common
events.summary: British researchers say rates of type 2 diabetes are growing most among women under 40. The disease is often underdiagnosed in women or diagnosed too late to reverse the condition's progression.

events.title: Study: Obesity 'bigger cancer risk' than previously thought
events.summary: A new study has found that being significantly overweight could be responsible for more cases of cancer than previously known. Abdominal fat, in particular, increases the risk of cancer — especially among women.

events.title: FIFA warns against 'concerted effort' to undermine Gianni Infantino
events.summary: Pressure is mounting on the FIFA president Gianni Infantino after plans to sell a stake in the World Cup collapsed and fresh allegations emerged relating to his time at UEFA.

events.title: Eco wins: Hungary goes solar, marmots go viral and Rome gets an upgrade
events.summary: From Hungary's accidental solar revolution to marmot crowdfunding and a long-overdue upgrade for Rome's big snake, good news comes in strange packages this week.

events.title: Testosterone and fertility: the trade-off men aren't told about
events.summary: Testosterone is trending in gyms, on social online and in politics. US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth even wants troops screened for low testosterone. But taking supplements can shut down the body's natural production.

events.title: Drought threatens power supplies in Danube countries
events.summary: Droughts, heat and falling water levels in the Danube are hitting central and southeastern Europe hard. Hungary and Romania are experiencing an energy crisis — whereas countries like Bulgaria are better prepared.

events.title: Mata Hari: Celebrated dancer turns WWI spy
events.summary: Mata Hari enthralled Europe's elite with her beauty and performances. Accused of spying during World War I, she faced a French firing squad in 1917.

events.title: AfD threatens to cut funding for 'modern-thinking' culture
events.summary: The far-right party could win an absolute majority in Saxony-Anhalt's state election in September. Their cultural program denigrates Bauhaus, Holocaust remembrance culture and diversity in theater.

events.title: How Gianni Infantino rose to rule football
events.summary: Gianni Infantino is staying on as FIFA president despite growing pressure to step down. So who is football's most powerful man, why did UEFA and others turn against him, and how did he reassert his authority?

events.title: Why is Russia selling its gold?
events.summary: Russia has become one of the world's biggest sellers of gold over the past 12 months. It's an attempt to raise cash in the face of budget issues, but not necessarily a sign of a looming financial crisis.

events.title: The hidden problem with small modular nuclear reactors
events.summary: Mini nuclear reactors are seen as a flexible energy source. Their promise: abundant energy, cheap, clean and climate-friendly with lower water use. But do the numbers add up? We look at what's behind the SMR hype.

events.title: My sleep deprivation is your natural short sleep
events.summary: Every so often we hear of high-ranking politicians or CEOs claiming to get by on very little sleep — some as little as three hours a night. If they're not natural short sleepers, chances are they're heading for trouble.

events.title: AI ecosystem's 'circular' investment: risk or advantage?
events.summary: Amid talk of an AI sector bubble, one aspect is under scrutiny. Many big AI players are invested in smaller ones, who then buy the bigger firm's products. This brings risks and advantages.

events.title: South Sudan: How climate change can result in toxic water
events.summary: Years of flooding have resulted in disastrous water pollution in South Sudan's main oil region. As communities, scientists and health workers scramble for solutions, the long-term impacts of the crisis is yet to emerge.

events.title: Tennis star Sabalenka supports sport's new sex test policy
events.summary: The world number one women's tennis player supports the WTA's new sex testing rules. Others are more critical of the policy.

events.title: Philippine couple married in hip-deep floodwaters
events.summary: A Philippine couple tied the knot on Tuesday at a Catholic church swamped in hip-deep waters, as heavy rains had pummelled large parts of the country for a month.

events.title: US postal whistleblower warns thousands of midterm ballots could be lost
events.summary: A US Postal Service whistleblower has warned that millions of Americans could be prevented from receiving mail ballots ahead of November's midterm elections because of a rushed, new system ordered by President Donald Trump and due for launch Tuesday. Trump signed an executive order in March seeking tighter controls on mail voting, which he has repeatedly claimed is vulnerable to widespread fraud despite offering no evidence of misconduct on such a scale. France 24’s Kethevane Gorjestani takes a closer look.

events.title: Search continues for tunnel workers in Nepal floods
events.summary: Nepali authorities believe that the dozens of workers trapped in hydropower tunnels could still be alive, as some of the tunnels have chambers with air supplies. But rescue teams are still struggling, with difficult weather and heavy rains worsening the situation, reports France 24's Shahzaib Wahlah.

events.title: George Clooney, Robert Pattinson expected on the red carpet at Venice Film Festival
events.summary: Our film critic Emma Jones takes us through the highlights as the 83rd Venice International Film Festival kicks off this Wednesday.

events.title: Israel ‘organised and prepared’ to remove Gaza population if US gives green light, Katz says
events.summary: Israel is "organised and prepared" to remove Palestininians from Gaza "by every way possible", Defence Minister Israel Katz told reporters Wednesday, adding that there was no alternative "solution" to crisis. The Israeli government was simply waiting for the US to figure out where to take the displaced Gazans, he said.

events.title: Paradox of Balladur's legacy: 'Highly popular' Gaullist elite yet 'too far away from the people'
events.summary: Sharon Gaffney is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at Lancaster University. According to Foucart, Édouard Balladur’s political legacy mattered because he embodied a political model that was innovative and yet limited in scope and longevity. As PM under Socialist President François Mitterrand, Balladur helped demonstrate that ideological rivals could govern together under cohabitation while pursuing an ambitious programme of privatisation and economic reform. Yet Foucart argues that Balladur’s ultimately unsuccessful presidential campaign exposed a deeper transformation in French politics: technocratic competence, elite stature and institutional authority were becoming less electorally powerful than the ability to connect with ordinary voters.

events.title: Xi calls on Mideast nations to be ‘masters of their own affairs’ in rare Egypt visit
events.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on "the people of the Middle East" to oppose "externalinterference" and consider reshaping the region's security order during a visit to Egypt. The rare visit by the Chinese leader comes as Beijing aims to expand its influence in the region as the Iran war tests the reliability of the traditional US security umbrella in a vital geostrategic zone.

events.title: French president to open Bayeux Tapestry exhibition as he starts UK visit
events.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron begins a two-day visit to Britain on Wednesday, viewing the landmark Bayeux Tapestry exhibition with King Charles III and becoming the first EU leader to be hosted by Prime Minister Andy Burnham. The tapestry depicts the Norman conquest of England in 1066. In the post-Brexit era, "the loaning of the tapestry is a great example of French-British cooperation" said Burnham.

events.title: France's back-to-school challenges: Phones, payslips, pupils
events.summary: First day of school jitters are now behind most of France's 11.6 million pupils, but this "rentrée", or back-to-school period, is being marked by a number of challenges and changes: phone bans, concerns over sexual abuse, teachers' salaries, and 161,000 fewer students due to France's falling birthrate. We take a closer look in Entre Nous.

events.title: FRANCE 24 in Nepal: The unbearable wait for missing relatives
events.summary: In Nepal, the hope of finding survivors is fading daily. Bodies are piling up in morgues, and storage capacity is reaching its limit. For the relatives of the missing, the wait is unbearable. They go from one hospital to another, consult the lists of survivors and scrutinise the photos of unidentified bodies. FRANCE 24's special correspondents met with several of these families at the morgue of Kathmandu University Hospital.

events.title: 'Dangerous consequences': Iran warns US after alleged strike on wedding
events.summary: Iran has launched strikes towards US allies in the Gulf this Wednesday after US bombardment that Tehran said hit a wedding party, killing five people and wounding dozens. The latest escalation appears to have hardened the mood in the Islamic Republic, with authorities warning American allies in the region they're fair game.

events.title: French-Saudi ‘Dragon Ball’ theme park puzzles Japanese manga fans
events.summary: Plans to build a manga-themed park outside Paris have sparked excitement in France, one of the first Western countries to fall in love with Akira Toriyama’s iconic “Dragon Ball” franchise. Saudi bankrolling of the project, however, and the lack of response from Japanese licence holders, have raised eyebrows among experts and fans alike.

events.title: Macron set to unveil Bayeux Tapestry in 'once in a generation' UK loan
events.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron is set to assist in the unveiling of the Bayeux Tapestry as it goes on show in the UK as part of a historic loan to the British Museum on Wednesday. Macron is on a two-day visit to the UK where he will become the first EU leader to meet new Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Downing Street.

events.title: Nepal floods: Hundreds of unidentified bodies
events.summary: France 24's Shahzaib Wahlah reports from Kathmandu, Nepal, after visiting hospitals and morgues in the city struggling to cope with the influx of dead from the devastating floods that hit the country a week ago. Authorities have now begun taking DNA samples from the relatives of the missing in the hope of identifying the bodies as the hope of finding more survivors fades.

events.title: Germany investigates suspected power substation sabotage, Russia summons German envoy
events.summary: Two incidents that disrupted power distribution systems in Germany are being investigated for sabotage, authorities said Wednesday, while one of them was also being examined for possible terrorism links. Meanwhile Russia said it was summoning Germany's charge d'affaires after Berlin blamed Moscow for last month's attempted drone attack at Leipzig airport.

events.title: World's only female tetraplegic racing driver on 'making the most' of what she's got
events.summary: A pioneering British sportswoman who broke her neck in a car crash when she was 16 says that after the accident, she decided to make the most of what she'd got. Nathalie McGloin became the world's first and only female tetraplegic racing driver, racing against both able-bodied men and women. Her story is proof that both gender and disability are completely irrelevant when it comes to racing cars. She spoke to us about her life and her charity Spinal Track.

events.title: IMF reaches historical loan agreement with Senegal
events.summary: The IMF and Senegal have agreed on a new 2.2 billion-dollar loan programme to support financial reforms, a relief for the country after a huge amount of unreported debt recently came to light. The president has accused his predecessor of hiding the true state of the country's imbalanced budget deficit.

events.title: UNIFIL peacekeepers patrol south Lebanon, caught between Israel and Hezbollah
events.summary: Since this spring, about 6 percent of Lebanon has been occupied by the Israeli army. On the ground, around 600 French soldiers from the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) continue to patrol the zone. The delicate peacekeeping mission documents violations of UN resolutions by both Israel and Hezbollah, with its own future highly uncertain. Our France 2 colleagues report, with FRANCE 24's Florent Marchais.

events.title: Kenya shifts to electric cars as fuel prices soar 50%
events.summary: In Kenya, locally made eletric vehicles are gaining traction as fuel prices rise. As more and more Kenyans consider going electric, local firms are stepping up to assemble EV's domestically.

events.title: Illegal mining ravages Johannesburg neighbourhoods
events.summary: Some houses in one Johannesburg neighbourhood are in danger of collapse because of illegal mining. Known as Zama Zamas, around 34,000 illegal miners are thought to be working in South Africa, in the hope of finding gold and chromium. The mines they dig hollow out the ground, which causes buildings to collapse as well as frequent power outages.

events.title: Iran: US accused of hitting wedding party in latest strikes
events.summary: #Tehran says at least four people were killed and dozens more wounded in a #US strike on a town near in the south of #Iran, near the Strait of #Hormuz.

events.title: Military buildup seen in Ethiopia near Sudanese border
events.summary: A major military buildup has been observed on the Ethiopian side of the Sudanese border. It comes amid intensified fighting between the Sudanese armed forces and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Sudan and Ethiopia have both accused each other of supporting rebels within their borders.

events.title: FRANCE 24 in Nepal: In Bharatpur, authorities begin burying unidentified bodies
events.summary: In Nepal, the death toll continues to rise. Every day, new bodies are recovered, but many remain unidentifiable. Several days after the devastating floods, some are already in an advanced state of decomposition. Faced with the influx of remains, authorities have begun burying them without formal identification, primarily to limit health risks and the strong odours. FRANCE 24's special correspondents traveled to Bharatpur, in southern Nepal, to one of these burial sites.

events.title: Who is Trump's Venezuela go-between?
events.summary: PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, September 2: We look at papers' coverage of the shadowy Venezuelan magnate who brokered the Washington-Caracas oil deal. In other news, the Pacific Islands Forum wants to talk climate change, but China's anger at the presence of Taiwan is stealing the limelight. Finally, the Bayeux Tapestry is back in Britain after nearly a millennium, with perhaps some salacious secrets.

events.summary: Two truckloads of food aid destined for hungry families in South Kordofan state, Sudan, were destroyed in an aerial attack over the weekend, the World Food Progamme (WFP) said on Wednesday.

events.title: ‘Fight for humanity’: Avoiding a climate catastrophe means acting now

events.summary: The woman and the crew were treated for injuries. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he condemned the violence committed “by a handful of rioters.”

events.title: Trump says U.S. has struck deal with Venezuela to take control of 65 billion barrels of oil reserves
events.summary: President Donald Trump announced Friday that the U.S. had entered into an agreement with Venezuela to take control of the country’s 65 billion barrels of oil reserves.

events.title: Families wait in agony as Nepal floods leave hundreds missing
events.summary: A New York couple traveling to Mount Kailash is among 65 Americans missing after a catastrophic flood along the Nepal-Tibet border.

events.title: Harry and Meghan arrive for ‘extended’ stay in the U.K. six years after royal exit
events.summary: Prince Harry and Meghan arrived back in the U.K.  after six years in California, a source close to the family confirmed to NBC News.

events.title: Hundreds are missing after catastrophic flooding in Nepal wipes out whole towns
events.summary: Flash floods hit Himalayan mountain towns and villages, sweeping away vehicles, bridges and even buildings as people fled in terror.
